source_caption:
Frankie & Johnny (1991) is a tender romantic drama about two people trying to find love when life has given them plenty of reasons to be afraid of it.

Starring Al Pacino and Michelle Pfeiffer, the film follows Johnny, an optimistic cook who falls for Frankie, a waitress who has built walls around herself after being hurt in the past. Johnny sees a chance for something real between them, but Frankie isn’t ready to let someone into her life so easily.

Their relationship develops through small moments, awkward conversations, and the kind of uncertainty that comes with letting someone get close. Johnny’s openness clashes with Frankie’s fear of getting hurt again, making their connection feel messy and genuine rather than like a perfect movie romance.

Set against the streets of New York, the film finds beauty in ordinary people searching for companionship. Pacino and Pfeiffer bring warmth and vulnerability to two characters who are simply trying to figure out whether love is worth another chance.

source_details.title: Frankie & Johnny
source_details.synopsis: Frankie & Johnny is a 1991 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Garry Marshall and starring Al Pacino and Michelle Pfeiffer (in their first film together since Scarface). Héctor Elizondo, Nathan Lane and Kate Nelligan appear in supporting roles. The original score is composed by Marvin Hamlisch. The screenplay for Frankie & Johnny is adapted by Terrence McNally from his own off-Broadway play Frankie and Johnny in the Clair de Lune, which featured F. Murray Abraham and Kathy Bates.
